items.title: Centered smooth-plus-sublinear objectives
items.note: centered states the theorem with all hypotheses written out: F convex, x_* a minimizer, U open and convex, ψ convex and locally C^{1,1} on U (LocallyC11On U ψ: differentiable on U with locally Lipschitz derivative), γ finite convex positively homogeneous of degree one, F = ψ + γ(· - x_*) on U (disp/008), and every admissible run whose initial sublevel {F ≤ F(x_0)} is compact and contained in U; conclusion: F(x_k) → F(x_*), Euclidean dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0, and x_k → x_* if x_* is the unique minimizer. The last sentence ("Neither original summand is required to be minimized at x_*") is centered_summands_not_minimized: an instance of all hypotheses in which neither ψ nor γ(· - x_*) is minimized at x_*. The proof follows the paper (via the inward condition and Corollary art:radial-convergence); the library's centered_values/centered_iterates prove the value and iterate statements by a cocoercivity bound instead.
Hypothesis hrep : ∀ x ∈ U, F x = ψ x + γ (x - xstar).

centered is proved along this proof. Undisplayed steps stated in Lean: initial_value_gt (lines 144-145: g_0 ≠ 0 gives F(x_0) > F(x_*)), uniform_lipschitz_gradient (lines 145-149: a uniform Euclidean Lipschitz constant L for ∇ψ on compact K ⊆ U; the Lean proof takes one radius of uniform local Lipschitz continuity and the gradient bound on K, L = max(M, 2G/ρ), instead of subdividing segments, so it does not need convexity of K; the paper's Lebesgue-number argument is also correct), homogeneous_part_at_differentiable (lines 156-159: γ is differentiable at r_x with gradient g - ∇ψ(x), ∇γ(r_x)ᵀ r_x = γ(r_x), zero contribution to the inward remainder), and centered_inward_condition (lines 160-161: art:inward-condition on K with M = L max_K ‖r_x‖², θ = 1/2, lower bound from convexity). Line 162: Corollary art:radial-convergence with b = F(x_0). All hold as written.

Stated under the theorem's hypotheses, for an admissible run with compact initial sublevel in U, K = {F ≤ F(x_0)} (variable with its defining equation) and a uniform Euclidean Lipschitz constant L ≥ 0 of ∇ψ (coordinateGradient ψ) on K, at every x ∈ K and every 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1 (the whole inward segment [x, x_*] ⊆ K). The Lean proof bounds the derivative of the remainder along the segment by Lτ‖r_x‖² (Mathlib's image_norm_le_of_norm_deriv_right_le_deriv_boundary) instead of integrating.

items.title: Coercive homogeneous objectives
items.note: Hypotheses 1 ≤ n, F convex (finite), Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne F, coercive = Tendsto F (cocompact (Vec n)) atTop. Conclusion: 0 minimizes F and every minimizer is 0, and every R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F (arbitrary x_0, H_0, c_1, c_2: the last sentence of the theorem) has F(x_k) → 0 and x_k → 0 (disp/011). Proved as in the paper through Theorem art:centered with ψ = 0, γ = F; the library proves the iterate statement through the homogeneous potential. Not vacuous: absRun (built by oneDimRun) is an explicit admissible run on the coercive homogeneous F(x) = |x| on R (x_k = (-1/2)^k, H_k = (3/2)2^{-k}, α_k = 1, c_1 = 1/4, c_2 = 1/2); see the module's non-vacuity example.

homogeneous is proved along this proof: coercive_homogeneous_positive (lines 211-213: F(0) = 0 and F > 0 off zero), homogeneous_sphere_bound (disp/012), sublevels_compact_of_coercive (line 218), centered with ψ = 0, γ = F (lines 218-219), iterates_of_values (lines 219-220: the lower bound gives x_k → 0). The alternative of lines 220-221 ("the inward remainder is identically zero, so the radial convergence corollary applies directly") is homogeneous_inward_condition (M_η = 0) and homogeneous_via_radial. All hold as written.

Under the theorem's hypotheses: the minimum of F over the Euclidean unit sphere {‖euclideanVector x‖ = 1} exists (IsLeast of the image), and the minimum μ satisfies μ > 0 and F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖ for all x. The facts F(0) = 0 and F > 0 off zero, proved before the display, are derived rather than assumed.

items.title: Compact homogeneous models
items.note: One theorem per case, each with the conclusion of Theorem art:homogeneous (0 is the unique minimizer; every admissible run, from every admissible start, has F(x_k) → 0 and x_k → 0) in its setting n ≥ 1. Norm: N : Seminorm ℝ (Vec n) with N x = 0 → x = 0. Gauge: F convex, PositiveDegreeOne, {F ≤ 1} bounded. Linear maximum (disp/013): a : Fin m → Vec n and F x the greatest of the a_iᵀx (IsGreatest of the range; no affine intercepts), {F ≤ 0} bounded. BfgsArticle.HomogeneousModels states the same three cases (norm_conclusion, gauge_conclusion, finiteMaxLinear_conclusion, with a Finset of slopes). Not vacuous: |x| on R is a norm, a gauge with bounded unit sublevel and the linear maximum max(x, -x), and absRun is an admissible run for it (also as normSeminorm ℝ (Vec 1)).

The three cases are proved along this proof: positivity off zero (norm axioms; for the gauge and the maximum, boundedness of the stated sublevel via Homogeneous.positive_of_bounded_zero_sublevel, the ray argument), sphere_minimum and coercive_of_lower_bound (F(x) ≥ μ‖x‖, hence coercivity), maxLinear_convex_homogeneous (finite maxima of linear forms are finite, convex and degree-one homogeneous), then Theorem art:homogeneous. All hold as written.
